chunks.arabic_text: سَهْلُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ [بِنْ أَحْمَدَ] بْنِ سَهْلٍ، الدِّيبَاجِيُّ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ. كَانَ ضَعِيفًا، يَضَعُ الْأَحَادِيثَ. وَيَرْوِي عَنِ الْمَجَاهِيلِ. وَلَا بَأْسَ بِمَا رَوَاهُ مِنَ " الْأَشْعَثِيَّاتِ " وَبِمَا يَجْرِي مَجْرَاهَا، مِمَّا رَوَاهُ غَيْرُهُ.

translations.en: Sahl ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdullāh (ibn Aḥmad) ibn Sahl, al-Dībājī, Abū Muḥammad. He was weak, fabricating ḥadīths. He narrated from unknown narrators. There is no harm in what he narrated from al-Ashʿathiyyāt and what is of that type, and from what (people) other than him narrated of it.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Ḍuʿafāʾ* characterizes Sahl al-Dībājī as a weak narrator prone to fabrication (*tadlīs*) and reliance on unknown sources (*al-majāhīl*). However, it applies the principle of *al-ṣaḥḥa bi-ghayrihā* (correctness through others), validating his reports when corroborated by stronger chains in the *Ashʿathiyyāt* collection, reflecting the nuanced Shia methodology of evaluating individual narrators against the broader corpus.
en.seo_question: Who is Sahl al-Dībājī and what is his status in ḥadith sciences?
